title: Recruiter Call Prep: Lease Coordinator
block_types_note: Built from the Markdown source. COACH NOTE -> coach_only (the guidance is written about Harry, in the third person). STARTER -> field.starter, pre-seeded text he edits. FIELD -> field. SUMMARY -> the summary blocks.

blocks.body: A recruiter found you on LinkedIn and reached out. You didn't apply, so something on your profile caught their eye.

items: LEARN enough about the role and company to decide if you want it.
MAKE IT EASY for the recruiter to put you in front of the hiring manager.

blocks.body: You don't need to be an expert on leasing. You need to be curious, clear, and easy to talk to.

blocks.label: Are they at an agency or at the company itself?
Anything from their LinkedIn profile worth mentioning

blocks.title: Before the call
blocks.body: Reread your own LinkedIn profile. That's what they saw, so your intro should match it.

sections.title: What Will They Remember You For

blocks.body: Recruiters talk to a lot of people. When they describe you to the hiring manager, what's the one thing they'll say? Not a resume line. Something uniquely you.

blocks.title: Coach note: the hook
blocks.body: No starter ideas. Let him find it.
The recruiter will probably open with "tell me a little about yourself." Keep it to about a minute. Present, Past, Future.

blocks.label: My Present
blocks.starter: I'm [where you are right now: school, grad, current job], and [one line on what you're interested in].

blocks.label: My Past
blocks.starter: [One or two things that got you here. Not job by job.]

blocks.label: My Future
blocks.starter: I'm looking for a role where I can [what you want to learn or do], so when you reached out about this, I wanted to hear more.

blocks.body: Have two short stories ready in case they ask. Situation, what you did, how it turned out.

blocks.label: A time you kept track of a lot of details and didn't let anything slip
A time you had a tight deadline and got it done

blocks.body: This is where you learn if you want the job. React to each answer before asking the next one.

blocks.label: My questions, and the three I care about most
blocks.starter:
1. What specifically about my background caught your attention?
2. Can you tell me a little more about the team, and why this role is open right now?
3. Is there a formal job description you could send me?
4. What systems does the team use day to day, like a lease management system?
5. What do the hours look like? Is it pretty much 9 to 5, or does it change depending on what's going on?
6. What's the pay range for the role?
7. What are the next steps in the process?

blocks.title: Coach note: the questions
blocks.body:
Q1 tells him what the recruiter already likes about him; reuse it in later rounds.
Q4: if he hasn't used their system, the answer is "I haven't used that one yet, but I pick up new systems fast" plus a quick example.
Q7 replaces the next-steps line in the close.
Pay is fair game on a recruiter call. Ask it yourself (Question 6): "What's the pay range for the role?"

blocks.title: If they turn it back to you
blocks.body: "I'd want to be paid fairly for the market, but getting the right experience matters just as much to me right now."
Before you hang up, ask these two.

items: Is there anything about my background you'd want me to clear up?
When should I expect to hear from you?

blocks.body: After the call, send a short thank-you the same day.

blocks.label: My thank-you note
blocks.starter: Hi [Name], thanks for taking the time today. I enjoyed learning about the Lease Coordinator role, and I'm excited about next steps. Best, Harry

blocks.note: About a minute in total. Say it out loud once before the call.

items: React to each answer before your next question
